Our Story

The question behind it all

During the past few months, we started several ventures, and all of these ideas finally converged into one simple idea, and that became the new venture. After peeling off every layer, we asked one very simple question:

“What’s the role of a human in the world of AI?”🤔

That’s what we wanted to answer, and this is our perspective.

The world we’re building in

AI is becoming dominant 🤖 in both the virtual and physical worlds. Every day, new brands are forming and existing brands are deploying new ventures or new features. Even the incumbents are struggling to maintain their position.

The one thing that stays human

While all of that is happening — while intelligence is being outsourced to machines — humans will retain one thing, and that is for sure.

The purchase decision for a product/service in any economy or any industry will always come back to a human. That means whatever products or services are developed or manufactured using AI, from whatever brand, that product or service needs to be sold to a human, and a human will make the final decision to purchase. 🫵

That is confirmed. ✅

Otherwise, the entire economy would not exist.

The insight

The best insight 💡 in all of this efficient, productive, and fast-moving world is that humans will always prefer to purchase something recommended by another human.

Of course, AI shopping agents will play a big role in purchasing decisions. But when it comes to shopping agents, cost is the only non-human variable that will affect a purchasing decision — an AI agent will find the most cost-effective solution. All other variables, like reviews, hype, trends, and quality, are human perceptions that will affect the purchase decision.

The opportunity

What if people could build brands around themselves? ✨

Think about it. Anyone can pick a field they care about — even a small, niche one — and start sharing their honest opinions about it. Over time, they build a community of people who trust them. They become the go-to expert. And once people trust someone’s judgment, that person can genuinely help others decide what to buy in that field — which makes them exactly the kind of ambassador the brands in that space are looking for.

Today we call this the influencer market, or the creator economy. It’s not new. But we think the word “influencer” needs a new meaning.

Influencers already carry more weight than ever. Across every market, they’re taking on real responsibility — and driving more of a brand’s sales than most people realize.

And who counts as an “influencer” is changing too. It’s no longer just lifestyle creators. Lawyers, doctors, and specialists are becoming creators for the brands they work with, and they bring something a typical influencer can’t: real credibility and authority.

We believe influencers will be at the center of the future economy. The next service industry will be built on them. Right now, this layer between brands and their customers is messy and unorganized. But soon, every person will have their own store — or their own AI agent — to serve their community. A personal storefront of their own. 🏪

What we’re building

This isn’t about building a personal online store. That’s just the tip of the iceberg — the part people see.

Underneath it, there’s a bigger engine at work.

Brands need a way to openly find the right influencers — not a handful, but thousands per brand. So we’re building that. It starts by verifying two things about every influencer: that they’re a real human, and that they’re an actual customer of the brand. Then a smart matching system pairs the right influencers with the right brands, so the people making recommendations actually know and use the products. That means a better experience for the end customer, too.

Put simply, it’s an automated way for brands to recruit influencers at scale — a marketplace that connects influencers with brand campaigns, powered by a recommendation engine that keeps improving the matches. And all of it feeds back into each influencer’s own personalized store.

Here’s the big shift: e-commerce used to be a funnel — one path, one store, everyone pushed toward the same checkout. Now it’s more like a strainer, with thousands of small outlets, each run by an influencer, each pouring customers in from a different direction.

We believe this needs to be a layer built on top of aggregating existing social media platforms and new AI assistants.

This is our perspective of the future ☝️ — unless AI kills us all. 🗿

Content Review, Approval, and Disputes

When a Campaign Owner approves a submission, the Creator earns the base payout and any performance pay. If the Campaign Owner does not approve or reject within 48 hours, the Platform may auto-confirm payment, provided the Content followed the Campaign Owner’s guidelines. A Campaign Owner may still raise a dispute after auto-confirmation; disputes go to a special Platform inquiry, and the Platform’s decision is final. Rejected or unpaid Content stays fully owned by the Creator.

Payments, Fees, and the Wallet

The Platform holds a Campaign’s full budget before it begins and pays it out as Content is approved and confirmed; any leftover budget is refunded to the Campaign Owner with no fee. The Platform takes a 10% commission on each Creator transaction, inclusive of all charges, so the Creator receives the balance. Campaign Owners pay no platform fee, but a 3% payment-processing charge applies to campaigns funded through an online gateway (not to bank transfers) and is borne by the Campaign Owner.

Earnings are made available through the Wallet, and a Creator may cash out once per day, via internet payment gateway or bank transfer. Bank details are used only for deposits and never shared. No tax is withheld from earnings; if any deduction is required, the Creator is notified on the transfer confirmation page beforehand. Each user handles their own tax obligations.

Performance-Based Pay and View Measurement

Performance pay is based solely on views, measured through the official APIs of the relevant social media platforms via OAuth. Only metrics each platform permits, within the scope the Creator authorizes, are accessed. The method or rate may change, with notice. To earn and keep payment, a Creator’s post must stay online and public until the Campaign ends (or any period the Campaign Owner sets). If it is taken down, made private, or removed before then, the Creator is not paid for that Content and must resubmit it as a new transaction.

Content Ownership and Copyright

Creators own the Content they create and publish, and may always keep it on their own channels and reuse it in a portfolio. Where a Campaign expressly requests raw Content and payment is completed, copyright in that Content transfers to the Platform — whether it received a base payout only or also performance pay. After transfer, the Platform may use the Content on its own channels; the Campaign Owner may use it only with the Platform’s consent; and neither may sell it to a third party. If a Creator is not paid, copyright stays fully with the Creator and none of these transfer rights apply.

Creator Status

Creators are independent contractors (freelancers). Nothing here creates an employment, agency, partnership, or joint-venture relationship with the Platform or any Campaign Owner, and Creators have no authority to bind either.
